question: The focal length of a convex mirror is:
solution:
The correct answer is **__positive__.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Focal length**

 
 
• The focal length of a mirror or lens is the distance between its** focal point and its pole**, also known as the **optical center of the lens.**
 
• After reflecting in the mirror, a **parallel beam of light** is "focused" at the focal point (F) of the device.
 
• In the case of a** convex mirror** and lens, the focal length is regarded as **positive.**
 
• It is considered a **negative for a concave mirror **and lens. The letter f denotes it.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Convex mirror**

 
 
• **​**A convex mirror is a kind of **spherical mirror** in which the reflecting surface is part of the sphere that is **bulging out** toward the incident light source.
 
• Convex mirrors always produce** virtual, erect, and diminished** images regardless of the distance between the object and the mirror.
 
 
 
• **Concave mirror**
 
 
• A mirror with its** inner surface** serving as the reflecting surface is created when a **hollow sphere **is cut into pieces and its outer surface is painted. A concave mirror is a name given to this kind of mirror.
 
• A **virtual, magnified image** is produced when the concave mirror is placed very close to the object.
